- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.33), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- After a sharp price spike (≥ 5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2–4% above peak for next 7 days.
- If model shows strong upward trend but true outcome shows mean reversion (price drops after peak), reduce forecast slope by 15–30% for next 10 days.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5–7 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overestimate early in the horizon (first 7–10 days); apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% per day for first 7 days.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (±0.33), model often fails to capture volatility; add ±1–2% volatility buffer to forecast range.
